title: Clarissa Nada Dahjan
text: Hi readers! My name is Clarissa, I am originally from Indonesia and came to Vancouver in 2019 to do my Bachelor’s degree in Mathematics at UBC. After graduating in 2023, I worked as a Data Analyst and Developer at DarkVision Technologies for 3 years. I am now returning to UBC to join the Master’s of Data Science program (2026-2027), hoping to enhance my hard skills in data science and analysis to be more confident when returning to data-related roles.

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with Python)
text:
Introduction
In this blog post, we will be investigating whether sex is associated with the size of penguins using Python. We will use the palmerpenguins dataset and compare physical measurements between male and female penguins.
We will answer this analysis question by examining the male-female ratios of penguin body mass, flipper length, bill length, and bill depth.

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with Python)
text:
Setup
Before proceeding, we will load the pandas package and the palmerpenguins package for the dataset.

import pandas as pd
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

Additionally, we will clean the dataset to remove any NA values before processing to avoid ambiguity.

penguins = load_penguins()
penguins_clean = penguins.dropna(subset=["sex", "body_mass_g", "flipper_length_mm"])

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with Python)
text:
Comparing Penguin Size by Sex
Below, we are calculating the average physical measurements for male and female penguins.

penguins_clean.groupby("sex").agg(
    mean_body_mass=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
    mean_flipper_length=("flipper_length_mm", "mean"),
    mean_bill_length=("bill_length_mm", "mean"),
    mean_bill_depth=("bill_depth_mm", "mean")
).reset_index()

The table allows us to compare the average measurements between male and female penguins. We can see that the values skew towards the male species of penguins.

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with Python)
text:
Comparing Size Within Species
Because different penguin species have different typical sizes, we can also compare males and females within each species.

penguins_clean.groupby(["species", "sex"]).agg(
    mean_body_mass=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
    mean_flipper_length=("flipper_length_mm", "mean")
).reset_index()

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with Python)
text:
Conclusion
The tables allow us to compare the physical measurements of male and female penguins, both overall and within each species.
If the average measurements are consistently larger for males, this provides evidence that sex is associated to some degree with penguin size in this dataset. Further statistical analysis could be used to determine whether the observed differences are statistically significant.

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with R)
text:
Introduction
In this blog post, we will be investigating whether sex is associated with the size of penguins using R. We will use the palmerpenguins dataset and compare physical measurements between male and female penguins.
We will answer this analysis question by examining the male-female ratios of penguin body mass, flipper length, bill length, and bill depth.

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with R)
text:
Setup
Before proceeding, we will load the tidyverse package and the palmerpenguins package for the dataset.

library(tidyverse)
library(palmerpenguins)

Additionally, we will clean the dataset to remove any NA values before processing to avoid ambiguity.

penguins_clean <- penguins |> drop_na(sex, body_mass_g, flipper_length_mm)

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with R)
text:
Comparing Penguin Size by Sex
Below, we are calculating the average physical measurements for male and female penguins.



Table 1: Average physical measurements of penguins by sex.


penguins_clean |>
  group_by(sex) |>
  summarise(
    mean_body_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_flipper_length = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_bill_length = mean(bill_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_bill_depth = mean(bill_depth_mm, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# A tibble: 2 × 5
  sex    mean_body_mass mean_flipper_length mean_bill_length mean_bill_depth
  <fct>           <dbl>               <dbl>            <dbl>           <dbl>
1 female          3862.                197.             42.1            16.4
2 male            4546.                205.             45.9            17.9




The table allows us to compare the average measurements between male and female penguins. We can see that the values skew towards the male species of penguins.

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with R)
text:
Comparing Size Within Species
Because different penguin species have different typical sizes, we can also compare males and females within each species.



Table 2: Average physical measurements of penguins by sex and species.


penguins_clean |>
  group_by(species, sex) |>
  summarise(
    mean_body_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_flipper_length = mean(flipper_length_mm, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# A tibble: 6 × 4
  species   sex    mean_body_mass mean_flipper_length
  <fct>     <fct>           <dbl>               <dbl>
1 Adelie    female          3369.                188.
2 Adelie    male            4043.                192.
3 Chinstrap female          3527.                192.
4 Chinstrap male            3939.                200.
5 Gentoo    female          4680.                213.
6 Gentoo    male            5485.                222.




This table allows us to determine whether the differences between males and females are consistent across species. We, again, see that this skewing pattern towards males are still true when we analyze it by species.

title: Palmer Penguins Analysis (with R)
text:
Conclusion
The tables allow us to compare the physical measurements of male and female penguins, both overall and within each species.
If the average measurements are consistently larger for males, this provides evidence that sex is associated to some degree with penguin size in this dataset. Further statistical analysis could be used to determine whether the observed differences are statistically significant.

title: About
text:
Why Data Science
In the 3 years at DarkVision, I was focused on honing my practical skills on using various Python functionalities to manipulate and process data. Although practical skills are useful, I felt like I was lacking in the theoretical knowledge and the “why” in some design decisions the team made for certain initiatives. Returning back to school for Data Science felt like the right move to take a step back and revisit concepts that I may be familiar with applying, so that it is strengthened with the theories behind them.
